Every fix in this lab so far has come from tracing a chain of dependencies that wasn't
visible until something broke: volume meaning different things for different models, a
mean-based price sitting next to a P90-based cost, a "risk score" that only touches three
of the five models. This page draws that map out up front.

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading the diagrams
**Solid arrows** are real dependencies — implemented in `comparator.qmd`'s code today, and
you can move the corresponding slider and watch the number change. **Dashed arrows** are
*conceptual* links — relationships that plausibly should exist given how the reference doc
and the rest of this site talk about risk and variability, but which the model currently
treats as independent sliders. They're flagged here as a map of where the model is
simplified, not a defect list.
:::

The full picture was one dense diagram; it's split into two smaller ones below — **drivers**
(the qualitative/shared inputs) and **computation** (how those drivers turn into price, cost
and margin) — so each stays readable on its own.

## Known gaps (dashed edges above)

These are places the model treats inputs as independent when a real pricing conversation
probably wouldn't — flagged here rather than fixed, since each is a judgement call about
how much realism this teaching tool needs versus how many more sliders it should have.

| Gap | What's missing |
|---|---|
| Task complexity → Token CoV | `m3Complexity` scales M3's *price*, but has no effect on either model's token-cost variability, even though a more complex task plausibly has a fatter-tailed token distribution too. |
| Risk score → per-unit risk premiums | The shared `riskScore` slider drives the generic overlay (M1, M2 T1, M4), but M2 Tier 2 and M3 have their own, entirely independent risk-premium sliders. Moving the shared risk score does nothing to them. |
| Token CoV / P90 → M5's floor | `token-distribution.qmd` explicitly teaches "set the floor on the P90/P95 cost, not a flat percentage" — but M5's actual floor is `0.8 × M4 base fee`, with no connection to any token-cost distribution at all. |
| Deployment tier → default recalibration | Switching tiers changes which models are *shown*, but doesn't adjust any default slider values — a Tier 3 (Digital Labor) scenario and a Tier 1 (Internal Use) scenario keep the same defaults even though the underlying engagement shape is usually very different. |
